# Source and local changes

- Klepton `https://github.com/shinyquagsire23/Klepton`, revision `1fe7e6caf6bb8bc90c1a5e61d5b9bfc6e110fa32`, MIT, copyright Max Thomas; its license is `LICENSE`. Only two pinned upstream files were retrieved, not a complete source archive: `upstream/kl_openxr.c` SHA-256 `223e361f5b3f629e27248131cd955ae5ae2b9f370a4e4f81d783b6f4242ff2b3` and `upstream/kl_openxr.h` SHA-256 `1f2d6a3f78f9ddcf64597a32aaffb2bb922d131fcdabdaaf9e0a5b35259df26c`. License SHA-256 `8705e40805c9267df365b89ceaa34a56498e34b7d3b6ebb95e9c12a7d3827a2b`.
- `src/core.c` is a selective adaptation, not the whole upstream file. `klxr_two_call` is taken from upstream lines 1056–1069 (names map to Khronos errors). `klxr_CreateInstance` follows lines 1262–1302 with zero advertised extensions, host configuration gate and bounded non-reused handles replacing the singleton. `klxr_GetSystem` follows lines 1327–1342, with actual host availability instead of unconditional presence. Dispatch adapts lines 718–739 and 6613–6753; unknown entries return errors rather than upstream's aborting stubs. Normal builds refuse session support; a partial test-only Metal resource/session slice is described below. Production session, action state and tracked input are not implemented. This inventory records local transformations in lieu of a patch directly applicable to the full upstream file. Instance/system properties follow upstream lines 1310–1391 but identify the actual partial runtime and take all device, limits, and tracking fields from a host callback rather than synthetic Quest defaults. Path interning and reverse lookup adapt upstream lines 3284–3318, with per-instance ownership, stale-ID protection, and full path-grammar validation added. Action-set bookkeeping adapts lines 3260–3274 and 3320–3359 with owner, unique-name and stale-handle checks. The Metal resource/session slice adds local code behind test-only `KL_NATIVE_TEST_METAL_PARTIAL`; production withholds the extension. Typed refusal functions are generated from official Khronos prototypes to avoid ABI-mismatched abort stubs. Local `core.c` SHA-256 `f4caa7ab17014be380a6e18dd634fcfd45a3e871a354d95faf15865d7cccd842`; refusal functions `70036549faaec37341dfc2834931c2caf5982ecc0d1b61465ec324a5c3f41a9b` and dispatch `76a4ea21274295e8f52230eb4adc250f580861b6fac84897443dd237ed7b4aed`.
- Khronos `openxr.h` and `openxr_platform_defines.h` were copied from the already-local `openxr-sys` 0.13.1 Cargo package's bundled `OpenXR-SDK/include/openxr`. Its lockfile package checksum is `4b8d66081de28c2fa40216182a37292fe38aeea20bc184612504d5e64daf5359`; crate VCS metadata gives openxrs repository commit `f50cf13afc047f96d540d9d85a08e023e0d3647d` (not an independently established OpenXR-SDK commit). Header declares API 1.1.54. Header SHA-256 respectively `d8bc0c759dbecfbd29901418f809d919f2d1ab6c710ab5fdf5205766fb92910b` and `59a5369c34013beeea505aa0465768acad558ac016bab3320780e2a653a07bfb`. Headers say Apache-2.0 OR MIT; the bundled OpenXR-SDK Apache license is retained in `OPENXR-SDK-LICENSE`, SHA-256 `cfc7749b96f63bd31c3c42b5c471bf756814053e847c10f3eb003417bc523d30`. Their Khronos copyright notices remain in the files.

- `openxr_platform.h` from the same `openxr-sys` package is retained for official Metal extension structures; SHA-256 `0da6b2ca34132704366236cebb9112dee85ae802c529476b902ecf4dcea278fd`. The retained Khronos Apache license and in-file alternative SPDX notice also apply.

- Session state adapts the upstream event/session lifecycle with an explicit host-driven state machine and acknowledged begin/end; it replaces synthetic READY with real host event callbacks and preserves running state on failed drain. Host adapter remains unimplemented.

- Swapchain acquire/wait/release ordering adapts Klepton FIFO behavior but delegates availability and write completion to a new explicit native host boundary. Timeout/failure preserves ownership, and destroy refuses acquired images. The table is not connected to a real host in this component.
- `src/pose_math.c` extracts quaternion/pose composition and relative-transform algebra from upstream `kl_openxr.c` lines 2405–2460, with new finite/unit-quaternion validation. SHA-256 `841bcc2b80e86435c25e81fe7d4138da49746cde86433eec9f8d27a63aa4dbdc`; it is linked into the provider for mock-tested reference-space transforms.

- View configuration enumeration follows upstream but gets separate recommended/max dimensions, sample counts and stereo/opaque support from explicit native host metadata; it never derives recommendations from maximums or invents a frame/pose.

The partial test lifecycle adds an optional host `request_exit` acknowledgment and explicit host `EXITING` event. Host STOPPING and EXITING represent actual logical session transitions; neither is inferred. The provider requires a successful request and completed drain before accepting EXITING. Session header SHA-256 `7ff099735cb5774fe3fff8f0dade323870e30def322ab393b55e54352e7454c5`.

Initially, pose action create/destroy bookkeeping adapted pinned upstream `kl_openxr.c` lines 3361–3384. Native changes add type restriction, name and owner/path validation, bounded non-reused handles, duplicate detection and child invalidation; POSE_INPUT and BOOLEAN_INPUT with left/right hand subaction paths are accepted. At that earlier checkpoint it did not implement action spaces, attachment, synchronization, tracked controller state or pose query.

The partial reference-space implementation accepts the standard XrSpaceVelocity output chain used by openxrs; no velocity samples are available, so the returned velocity flags are zero. Unsupported output chains remain refused.

- Action identity bookkeeping accepts the five OpenXR legacy action types (pose, boolean, float, vector2 and vibration), with stale handle and unsupported-type tests. At that earlier checkpoint binding, action state and haptic operations refused; identity alone does not assert active devices or input.

- Native input host v1 (`include/input_host.h`, earlier SHA-256 `55b83899218d26681045f3f10d0130ea197bb2e80534af509b11b2e49406fd9a`) and attach/sync support explicit host-observed disconnected hands only. Same-ID/time polls are accepted; rewinds and inconsistent IDs fail, as do connected hands. Other unsupported bindings and haptics still refuse. The macOS ARM64 UBSan `tests/metal_mock.c` covers attach order, repeated and conflicting samples, failed sampling, and connected-hand refusal; this is a host mock without headset or game.
- Native input host v2 is a separate sample and `kl_native_configure_input2`. Current header SHA-256 `c2dbeed50987dac85bad8aa410473397ac550ed40d01c592f554f1d160b5eaab`. A coherent connected sample makes `xrSyncActions` succeed. The interaction profile stays null and Boolean, Float, Vector2f, and Pose actions stay inactive, so no controller is created. A disconnected hand may not carry a tracked pose, a pressed button, or a finite analog. Trigger, when present, is 0..1; a stick is a pair in −1..1; NAN means that analog was not observed. Repeating one id with different controls fails. Version 1 and its connected-hand refusal are unchanged. The same macOS ARM64 and UBSan metal mock covers this. No profile, haptic, headset, or game is claimed.

- The four non-extension profiles used by xrizer legacy setup accept validated, instance-owned suggested bindings, which do not activate a profile. Attached actions return inactive Boolean, Float, Vector2f or Pose state only after a successful disconnected host sample; failed sync invalidates the sample and state queries fail closed. Connected devices remain unsupported. Owned boot and UBSan mock tests pass, including path/type rejection and stale-state refusal. Injected-host diagnostic vMt8Z7 observed all four actual xrizer suggestions and attach succeed, but sync returned XR_SESSION_NOT_FOCUSED; that snapshot did not verify actual focused state or tracking.

- `tests/xrizer_pose_probe.m` and `test-xrizer-pose-probe.sh` are an owned native-host diagnostic. The earlier diagnostic runner removed three guards only in its sealed snapshot; that bypass was not an accepted runtime configuration. The current runner uses unchanged compositor source after the guards were removed in the tested owned route. With injected focused lifecycle, disconnected input and changing tracked head samples, snapshot 2AhwXe passed four actual native xrizer calls including invalid tracking, role/state and pose-array controls and clean cancellation. It does not prove a Windows guest, real input/tracking, headset, or game. Snapshot manifest SHA-256 `2db388d73b855d1985d8b2dea838b68b9edb54a75d898340b59789cc118133ac`; changed-source record `e336bad843c8d2037406541845a8f96ab56272ffbe800c2a67d48971418765bf`; log `4d59d0fbf58e3a7081fa1e9a4940090dce1de7c67b67fda5bf5b0d5a2629fdeb`.

- Final-source owned-apple-test snapshot aZWPby makes no compositor edits: manifest `3b16d9f8bafb0ffaea077329415855eb24adb8ceff758bae5f3cf7ee78297110`, fixture-only substitution record `3fdbb0f4aabb60a8de53559da494be97b9b8e467d9a5f8fb9aba35d8bca00e7e`, dylib `89fcbe65fdb6862b8a21a6bef68b6acdf8f47adec92d067c283b31707287a78c`, log `76668681475c20c705bd6434ae2e588709b5c308b25885eead0190e160b3dcad`, execution environment `acfb543bf33e966812b082f52abcc1229b5d6f722598afc7519cd25c8e68937a`. The test still injects host focus, tracking and disconnected hands and makes no physical or Windows guest claim.

- Expanded final-source owned snapshot Un4dP4 passed disconnected controller-with-pose/haptic and System device-pose array/null controls in addition to the earlier four-frame test. Manifest `6fbe011294d1367849693e214675e16ecfc00b01b82eae9d7084df72b9840ff0`, native dylib `5853797da60b4f46d5734f7c799df79e7bc3526e84bddc2aeebac4fa94aaa567`, log `92c3db2ef9d9923772bd8f4267f36be4226021422c526cb3f320e56df88e6d5a`; macOS ARM64, injected host, not a guest or physical test.

- Versioned static optical geometry (`include/view_host.h`, SHA-256 `329a51ba840b2ba842dae76d4f17a03dbdc0b816edf0d5552193a7f71b53ee7f`) is a private provider query through the registered native dispatch, not an OpenXR extension. It validates nonzero generation, finite unit eye poses and finite ordered FOV, without creating a frame or providing tracking. macOS ARM64 UBSan owned `views.c` tests callback and malformed/missing data controls. Actual native xrizer owned fixture snapshot `0szp4u` passed pre-Wait injected eye/projection goldens with no tickets, post-Wait geometry, four valid/invalid tracked-head samples and disconnected hands with four cancellations, exit 0; source manifest SHA-256 `1226df3eb568214eda0abd47a3e6a1a970564222198a8da2ed4dcca0dd3d0888`, diagnostic fixture substitution record `01b686e7d7e31944dd71d86eb38dfa9edcf869de223a84a8257da4d2f5f72e36`, log `306e5f732bbb4aca974595d8fd2f2aa3d70c69a688a5bb006ef235cd86ec7d78`, xrizer dylib `19f93f9e1bceace03ddfd7e999f33130df77d39fe2d85d04973fd54f187f8262`. Separate frontend snapshot `46TahC` returned Init 150 for missing, invalid, or failed geometry, with zero frame waits; ready bootstrap passed. These are injected native-host controls, not Windows guest, physical tracking, headset, or game evidence.

- Input host version 3 (`include/input_host.h`, SHA-256 `5c4c03eeccfc647f108356c3ba358f139eae473f6ffa519e321f4895bfe6ec67`): a version-2 hand plus the host's controller kind (Oculus Touch, Index, Vive or simple) and the hand's grip and aim poses in LOCAL. `xrSyncActions` makes that profile current for a hand only when the application suggested bindings for it and queues one `XrEventDataInteractionProfileChanged` per change; `xrGetCurrentInteractionProfile` reports it; bound Boolean/float/vector controls of a connected hand become active with the sampled values (touch/force components are not observed and stay inactive; `lastChangeTime` is the sync's sample time for a change seen at that sync and 0 otherwise); `xrCreateActionSpace` (refused before, and still refused with version 1/2 hosts) locates a pose action at the bound grip/aim pose of the last successful sync, valid and with tracked bits only when the host says so (and-ed with the base space's flags, so LOCAL drops them), without prediction or velocity. A disconnected hand must carry no profile and all-zero poses. Owned macOS ARM64 `metal-mock` (plain and UBSan) covers suggestion gating, the event, active states and `changedSinceLastSync`, action-space location, an unsuggested profile, a malformed disconnected hand and the version-2 refusal; `build-test.sh` exit 0 including the visionOS simulator/device cross-compiles. Used by the VXRuntime offscreen dev host's opt-in synthetic controllers (`VXRT_XRIZER_DEV_CONTROLLERS`), a diagnostic; no physical controller, tracking or haptics.
